extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, naturalists, specialists in biology and zoology)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative review of scientific books, monographs, and experimental reports in biology/natural history, discussing experimental methods, illustrations, taxonomy, bibliography, and fieldwork methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of sterilisation/heat treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: "The heat employed in the sterilising process must be adequate to kill all pre-existing living things within the experimental vessels."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report and justify sterilisation parameters (temperature, time). The review notes Bastian heated fluids to 115°C–130°C for 10–20 minutes and cites a Pasteur Institute subdirector's claim that "a temperature of 115° C. sterilises [spores] completely and most rapidly." Evaluate whether sterilisation was sufficient to eliminate spores and other resistant forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention of subsequent contamination
rubrics_metrics.description: "There must be no subsequent contamination with atmospheric germs."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe measures to prevent contamination (hermetic sealing, sterile handling). Check for possible contamination during preparation of slides and cover-slips and during photography; document controls that rule out ingress of external germs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of sterilisation/sealing side-effects (medium degradation, exclusion of actinic rays)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The degrading effect of the initial purifying heat process may render the medium unfit... and the glass of the hermetically sealed vessel... partially excludes actinic rays which might be potential... in bringing about the combinations in question."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether sterilisation or containment procedures alter the experimental medium or remove essential environmental factors (e.g., actinic/UV radiation). Design experiments that account for or control such side-effects and justify choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and unambiguity of photomicrographic evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: "Some of the photomicrographic figures of 'organisms' are not very like organisms..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, unambiguous micrographs; avoid or identify artifacts. Ensure images are diagnostic and accompanied by scale, description, and handling notes to allow assessment of whether structures are biological or artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit consideration and listing of alternative interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: Review enumerates alternative readings: "(i) that Dr. Bastian's methods were not rigorous enough; (2) that the fatal temperature has been estimated at too low a figure; (3) that contamination occurred during the preparation of the photographed slides, or (4) that archebiosis actually takes place."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claiming novel phenomena, explicitly state and evaluate alternative explanations (methodological failures, incorrect parameter estimates, contamination, artifacts) and show how they are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental rigour, reproducibility, and burden of proof for extraordinary claims
rubrics_metrics.description: "We are not disposed to accept the last interpretation until every possibility of error has been excluded... Until we have seen for ourselves."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extraordinary claims require exhaustive controls and independent replication. Authors should design experiments to be reproducible and provide sufficient methodological detail so others can attempt verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth versus breadth of treatment (thorough case studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: "He does not go thoroughly enough into any single instance to win conviction."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For sweeping theoretical claims, include detailed, in-depth case studies rather than only broad, superficial coverage. Going thoroughly into single examples strengthens persuasion and evidential support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of concrete illustrations and examples to support abstract claims
rubrics_metrics.description: "In a popular elusive manner, with abundant concrete illustrations, the author seeks to show..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support abstract theoretical discussion with abundant, concrete examples and illustrations that clarify and substantiate claims; concrete cases make general arguments more convincing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of intemperate or dogmatic assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticises sweeping statements such as "life is an aquatic phenomenon" or "the self of being conscious does not intervene..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain scientific restraint; avoid overreaching generalisations not fully supported by evidence. Tone should be measured and claims proportionate to the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, precision, and elegance of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Several passages criticised as lacking precision or elegance: "This lacks precision. This lacks elegance. This lacks clearness."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write with precise, clear language; avoid ambiguous or clumsy formulations. Ensure statements are well-defined and terminology used consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality, accuracy, and correspondence of illustrations/plates to the text
rubrics_metrics.description: "These are models of what such illustrations should be... there is something wrong with Figs. 127 and 128... the letters of the former not corresponding with the description, and the number of joints... not coinciding with the statement in the text."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures and plates must be clear, accurate, and correctly labelled; legends and figure labels must correspond exactly to text descriptions. Errors in figures are blemishes and should be avoided or corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of bibliography and accuracy of references
rubrics_metrics.description: "This work does not include a bibliography, and such references as are given are not always to the point..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a full bibliography and ensure references are accurate (correct series, volume, page). Accurate citation allows readers to verify claims and follow prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of systematic and subject indexes
rubrics_metrics.description: Praise for containing "an excellent systematic index, a subject-index" in supplements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide systematic and subject indexes in extensive monographs to aid usability and retrieval of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field collection methodology and scientific thoroughness of exploration
rubrics_metrics.description: "If the locality chosen has shown exceptional richness, its exploration must have been conducted with a method and a science of the research of the species..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document collection methods, sampling efforts, and search strategies. Rigorous field methodology is necessary to justify claims about richness, new species, or faunal composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomic thoroughness and detailed specimen documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports include species counts, depths, variability notes (e.g., depths 0–43 fathoms; lists of species with new-to-science counts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed taxonomic descriptions, exact localities, depth ranges, specimen counts, and notes on variability. Such detail supports taxonomic decisions and subsequent use by specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative biogeographical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: "Compares the oceanic copepods of the Indian Ocean with those of the Atlantic... an intermixture of species ... being hindered by the water barrier formed by the Agulhas Current."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include comparative analyses with other regions, and explain physical or ecological barriers that affect species distributions; situate findings in broader biogeographical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and illustration of rare or novel specimens (including colour plates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: description of a rare squid "Ancistrochirus Usueufi, which has luminous organs... illustrated by folding plates."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing rare or novel specimens, provide high-quality illustrations (colour plates when appropriate) and detailed descriptions to document uniqueness and facilitate recognition.
